headline: New law has FEMA form an advisory group on disaster debris removal and orders a federal study of debris removal contracts.
what_it_does: The law tells FEMA to set up an advisory working group that helps people and organizations involved in disaster recovery work together on debris removal. FEMA must reach out to state, tribal, and local governments about any guidance or support materials it creates. The Government Accountability Office (GAO) must study how often state, tribal, and local governments sign debris removal contracts before a disaster happens.

who_it_affects.how: They will get outreach from FEMA about debris removal guidance, and their use of advance debris removal contracts will be studied by the GAO.

who_it_affects.group: Individuals and organizations that work on disaster debris removal
who_it_affects.how: They may take part in or work with a new FEMA advisory group meant to improve cooperation on debris cleanup.
The agency must create the advisory working group and conduct outreach on its guidance materials.
It must carry out a study on the use of advance contracts for debris removal.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 17, 2024; the summary does not list specific deadlines.
